aircraft.source: Publicly documented typical operating profile — manufacturer published specifications (service ceiling, Mmo, typical cruise Mach) plus standard airline operating procedure (250 KIAS below 10,000 ft per 14 CFR 91.117, typical climb speed schedule).
aircraft.source_confidence: TYPICAL PROFILE, NOT CERTIFIED PERFORMANCE DATA. Airbus AFM/FCOM climb and cruise performance tables are proprietary and not publicly available. This file describes what a normally-operated A321 is expected to do, which is a meaningful benchmark for 'did this flight fly a standard profile?' — but it is NOT a POH comparison and should not be labeled as one.

climb.reference_condition: Typical airline climb profile at moderate takeoff weight, ISA conditions. Speed schedule: 250 KIAS below FL100, ~300 KIAS climb, transitioning to M0.78 at crossover altitude.
climb.notes: Rates of climb for transport aircraft vary enormously with takeoff weight, which ADS-B cannot observe. A heavy A321 departing on a long sector may climb at half these rates. Treat wide deviations as expected, not as anomalies, unless weight is known.

cruise.reference_condition: Long range / typical economy cruise, ISA
cruise.notes: Typical operating Mach for the A321 is around 0.78, with 0.80 used when schedule recovery matters. Mmo is 0.82. Cruise Mach observed materially above 0.80 is worth a second look; below 0.76 suggests cost-index or ATC speed control.

descent.reference_condition: Typical idle-thrust descent, M0.78 / 300 KIAS / 250 KIAS below FL100
descent.notes: Typical airline descent planning uses roughly 3 nm per 1000 ft of altitude to lose, giving a nominal descent rate near -1800 to -2200 fpm at cruise speed.
